{{Quote|I ''am'' the Empire.|Roan Fel|<ref name="Legacy (2006) 8">[[Legacy (2006) 8|''Legacy'' (2006) 8]]</ref>}}
The '''Fel Empire''', also called the '''New Galactic Empire''', '''Galactic Empire''', '''Reborn Empire''', '''Fel Imperium''' or simply the '''Empire''', was a hereditary [[monarchy]] located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The Fel Empire was founded some time after [[44 ABY]] following the ascension of [[Jagged Fel]] to the [[Fel dynasty|throne]], and was formed from the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] and was ruled from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]].

The Fel Empire was ruled by the [[Fel dynasty]] and was assisted by the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]], used centralized rule, and eventually gained at least one [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]: [[Roan Fel]]. Rabidly [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] views among a minority persisted until the time of the [[Second Imperial Civil War]].<ref name="Legacy 20">[[Legacy (2006) 20|''Legacy'' (2006) 20]]</ref> However, unlike [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], a tyrannical [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] steeped in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] who ruled the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Fels encouraged the proliferation of [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] Force-users and peacefully spreading influence through the [[Victory Without War]] campaign, even forming a [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] analogue known as the [[Imperial Knight]]s and a charity program called the [[Imperial Mission]].

The Fel Empire became the dominant power in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by the conclusion of the [[Sith–Imperial War]], replacing the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], the successor state to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. However, the Fel Empire shortly fell. In its place, a new [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]] arose, forcing those loyal to the Fel dynasty into [[Empire-in-exile|exile]].

==History==
===Establishment===
{{Quote|If we're destroyed&mdash;if we all die&mdash;the concepts and ideals of the New Order will die with us. But if we surrender, we can keep those ideals alive. Then, if and when the New Republic self destructs, we'll be positioned to rise again.|[[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]]|<ref name="Specter of the Past">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Imperial-formation.png|thumb|right|300px|The Fel Empire (or New Galactic Empire) was the restoration of the First Galactic Empire (pictured) founded by Darth Sidious, which fell during the Galactic Civil War.]]

Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] and the death of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was toppled by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], now the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], and soon fell into [[Imperial Civil War|infighting]]; with several different offshoots and factions being formed to fill the void left over.

It is clear that the official name of the government under the [[Fel dynasty]] was anything other than the "Galactic Empire", as in c. [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] had emerged as the primary successor of the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Empire]] under [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], with military power being held by the surviving [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] of the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Moff Council]], in alliance with [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] as [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], with the relatively small fragment of territory it came to rule&mdash;though Imperial loyalists themselves usually spoke of "[[Imperial Space]]" and continued to refer to the Remnant as the "Galactic Empire" and "the Empire".

By the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the Imperial Remnant had become apart of the reorganized New Republic, now known as the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], allowing Gilad Pellaeon to succeed [[Sien Sovv]] as [[Supreme Commander (Alliance)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Galactic Alliance Defense Force]], signifying the level of cooperation and integration of the former galactic government with the new one, at least at that time period. The appointment of former Imperial General [[Turr Phennir/Legends|Turr Phennir]], however, as the Supreme Commander of the combined [[Confederation]] military may indicate the existence of secessionist sympathizers within the semi-autonomous Remnant.

[[File:JaggedFel-ERC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Fel dynasty began with the ascension of Emperor Jagged Fel to the throne, reviving the Galactic Empire.]]
At some point, following its participation in the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Imperial Remnant began to regain strength. [[Jagged Fel]], once again at the helm of the Empire, began the [[Victory Without War]] program to peacefully spread imperial influence, which consequently led to his assumption of the vacant title of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] many years later. This marked a partial restoration of the Galactic Empire with its' capital located on the planet [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]] in the Outer Rim, which subsequently became one of the most fortified [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the galaxy. Despite the Fel Empire officially being at peace with the Galactic Alliance, several [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] still held a distaste for the Galactic Alliance, leading to personal cold war-esque hatred that lasted for several decades.

===The Sith&ndash;Imperial War===
{{Main|Sith&ndash;Imperial War}}
[[File:RoanFel_EA.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The rule of Jagged Fel's Empire eventually passed to his grandson, Emperor Roan Fel.]]
Over a [[Standard century/Legends|century]] after the Battle of Endor, the [[One Sith]] sabotaged the [[Ossus Project]], a massive reconstruction effort employing [[Yuuzhan Vong]]-terraforming techniques to restore worlds devastated by the Vong War, to the detriment of the planets' inhabitants and killing millions in the process. The [[New Jedi Order]] and the Galactic Alliance soon found itself facing a secession movement mirroring that of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The Empire used this situation to entice Alliance member worlds to secede and become part of Imperial space. But the Empire wanted all of the Alliance worlds, including [[Coruscant/Legends|its capital]].

Eventually, the Moff Council, at the behest of [[High Moff]] [[Morlish Veed]] and [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Morrigan Corde|Nyna Calixte]], invoked the [[Treaty of Anaxes]] against the will of Emperor [[Roan Fel]], and in [[127 ABY]], the Sith-Imperial War broke out, and the One Sith allied with the Empire. The war resulted in the fall of the Alliance and the reestablishment of the Galactic Empire as the primary galactic government. The remnants of the Alliance were absorbed into the Empire, but the [[Core Fleet|Galactic Alliance Core Fleet]] remained, and continued to fight the resurgent Empire. Shortly after the fall of the Alliance, the Emperor called upon the entire New Jedi Order to surrender and subject their will to the Empire. Some of them did, becoming [[Imperial Knight]]s, while the others held to the will of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and retreated to [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]].

===The coup===
{{Main|Attack on Emperor Fel}}
{{Quote|Roan Fel ''never'' really embraced the war or the idea of a unified galaxy. He went along with it as a political necessity. That's not what the Empire&mdash;what the galaxy&mdash;needs. The galaxy writhes in chaos and disorder. It requires a man of vision. I am that man of ''vision''. ''I'' am the new Emperor.|Darth Krayt|<ref name="Legacy 1" />}}
[[File:DarthKraytEAtlas.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Darth Krayt usurped the Fel throne, becoming the first [[Sith Emperor/Legends|Sith Emperor]] to rule the galaxy since Darth Sidious.]]

After the Alliance defeat and the [[Massacre at Ossus]], the Sith under the command of [[Darth Krayt]] turned against Emperor Roan Fel. He launched a daring coup, marching with his cohorts straight into Fel's audience chamber himself, and killing [[Roan Fel's double|the man who sat on the throne]]. After the man's death, Krayt sat himself in his place. Noting the confusion and outrage from the members of the Moff Council who were present, he laid out the facts of life for them.

Faced with little choice, the Moff Council swore loyalty to the new Dark Lord of the Sith. For the first time since [[Darth Caedus]] during the Second Galactic Civil War ninety years prior, a Sith Lord held both sway over the Empire and the galactic seat of power. At once he set about imposing order on a galaxy that sorely needed it, but this too was an incomplete victory. The "Emperor" he had killed had been a double; the real Fel was a fully trained Imperial Knight and would surely have defended himself, rather than just stand there and let himself be slain. It was imperative that the real Fel be found before he recruited allies among the Moffs, the military, or those Jedi who had survived the massacre at Ossus.

===Insurgency and restoration===
{{Main|Second Imperial Civil War}}
Not all of the Empire recognized Darth Krayt's authority. Over the years, forces loyal to Fel gathered on Bastion, awaiting the return of their true Emperor. With the Imperial Knights leader [[Antares Draco]] and the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] commander [[General/Legends|General]] [[Oron Jaeger]] at his side, Fel took control of the planet in [[137 ABY]], knowing that Krayt would be wary to amass a frontal assault on the heavily fortified planet. With the Fel Empire a thing of the past, Fel led an [[Empire-in-exile]]. As the factions of Krayt and [[Empire-in-exile|Fel]] grew larger, units that once served with each other were now forced to fight against one another for control of territory around the galaxy.

==Government and politics==
{{Quote|I was tired of Fel playing us against each other!|Moff [[Geist (Moff)|Geist]]|<ref name="Legacy (2006) 15">[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]]</ref>}}
[[File:Fel_Empire_Troops.jpg|thumb|right|250px|For the first time, non-[[Human/Legends|Humans]] worked alongside Human soldiers in [[Imperial Military/Legends|the military]] of the Fel Empire.]]
The Fel Empire was ruled by an Emperor, a sovereign ruler for life, yet the Moff Council led by the Grand Moff held considerable power, and advised him. By all accounts, the reign of Roan Fel was relatively benevolent, and had far less of the abuses of power and tyrannical excesses of the Old Empire under Palpatine, though he was not above playing power games for the sake of maintaining his authority.

By the time of Fel's reign, the Empire's infamous bigotry against non-Human species had faded to the point that stormtroopers had aliens among their ranks and the Imperial Navy had at least one non-Human admiral, namely the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Sha Dun]].

The Moffs not only governed sectors, but also managed both the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] and [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]], as well as other institutions such as the [[Imperial Mission]] and the [[Imperial Diplomatic Corps/Legends|Imperial Diplomatic Corps]], and held enough power to invoke treaties and to launch wars. Still, some, such as Moff [[Geist (Moff)|Geist]], longed to return to the days when the Empire was under the complete control of the Council.

The [[Imperial Knight]]s were former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who, while technically remaining on the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|Light Side of the Force]], owed their loyalty to the Emperor rather than to the Force itself after the events of the Sith-Imperial War. They acted as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] to the Emperor, although they also had orders to immediately kill the Emperor should the latter irrevocably fall to the Dark Side.

==Astrography==
The Fel Empire's [[Imperial Space|territory]] originally consisted of a few "backwater" [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] that bordered the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], located in the northern quadrant of the galaxy. At some point following the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the Empire briefly gained further territories across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. However, the [[Sith–Imperial War]] saw most of the territories of the Empire alongside those of the Galactic Alliance, save a [[Empire-in-exile|few]] [[Galactic Alliance Remnant|worlds]], absorbed into [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[One Sith|Sith]]-controlled [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].

The capital of the Empire was originally [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]] but it was briefly moved to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], keeping in tradition with its original incarnation. However, Bastion continued to play an important role in Imperial affairs.

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars Insider 87|''Star Wars Insider'' 87]], [[John Ostrander]] describes the Fel Empire as "not as inherently evil [as the earlier Empire], but still not a republic, not a democracy. It's the rule of the few, or the one, over the many. It has a lot of strengths; it has a substantial amount of weaknesses. It values power more than anything else."
